/web-scraping-ai-agents-2026/.title: AI Agents for Web Scraping: API/XHR, Playwright
/web-scraping-ai-agents-2026/.description: AI agents for web scraping in 2026: API/XHR first, embedded JSON next, Playwright/browser agents for JS/auth, and LLM extraction only after verification.
/web-scraping-ai-agents-2026/.summaryHtml:
AI agents for web scraping: the 2026 stack

The best web scraping AI agent workflow is not agent-first. Start with official API or XHR JSON, check embedded JSON next, use Playwright or a browser agent only when JavaScript, login or interaction is required, and reserve LLM extraction for small reviewed cleanup.

LayerUse it forDo not use it for
API/XHRRepeatable data jobs, search results, product lists, comments, profiles and pagination.Private endpoints you cannot monitor or requests you do not understand.
Embedded JSONNext.js data, JSON-LD, hydration blobs and article metadata already shipped in HTML.Large recurring jobs without saved fixtures and schema checks.
Playwright or browser agentRendered pages, auth cookies, infinite scroll, forms, dashboards and consent flows.High-volume scraping where a stable API/XHR source exists.
LLM extractionOne-off cleanup from a small page, copied text, screenshot or PDF.Unverified production data, selectors, financial facts or personal data collection.

My rule: use the agent to inspect and choose the data source, then verify the rows and turn recurring extraction into boring code with logs, retries and tests.
/web-scraping-ai-agents-2026/.relatedHtml:
Next step: turn scraping into an AI-agent workflow

If this page saved you parser time, the broader stack lives in AI agents, MCP, AI tools and web scraping. For Claude Code-specific setup, start with MCP servers, hooks and skills.

For a Telegram-flavoured example of the same boundary, read the Telegram MCP Server guide. If you want the agent to keep running after the browser task is done, see my always-on AI agent server setup. External receipt: this workflow-vs-agent split is also the core of Nikita Belyaev's talk “What to leave to people, workflow and agent”.

Follow the practical AI-agent notes in Telegram
/web-scraping-ai-agents-2026/.faqHtml:
FAQ

What is the best web scraping AI agent workflow?

The best workflow is API/XHR first, embedded JSON second, browser automation third, raw HTML last. The AI agent is most useful as an inspector: it finds the cleanest source, documents the steps and helps turn recurring work into tested code.

Is web scraping dead in 2026?

No. One-off manual scraping is less common because agents can inspect pages quickly, but production extraction still needs stable sources, retries, monitoring, rate limits and clear legal boundaries.

Can AI agents replace web scraping?

They can replace many one-off scraping scripts, but not durable data pipelines. If the job runs daily, affects customers or feeds a database, use the agent for discovery and then ship tested extraction code.

When should I use Playwright or a browser agent instead of API/XHR?

Use Playwright or a browser agent when useful data appears only after JavaScript rendering, login, scrolling, form interaction or cookie consent. If a clean JSON endpoint exists, API/XHR remains simpler and more reliable.

Should I use Playwright or a scraping API for my AI app?

Use Playwright when the agent must interact with the site: login, click through filters, wait for JavaScript, inspect state and debug broken selectors. Use a managed scraping API when you need repeatable public-page extraction at scale, proxy handling, anti-bot retries or structured output as a service. For a durable AI app, I still start by checking API/XHR and embedded JSON before paying for either layer.

Can LLM extraction parse websites reliably?

LLM extraction is useful for small, reviewed, low-frequency tasks. It should not be the source of truth for large tables, finance, personal data or production jobs unless another check verifies the output.

What should be workflow, code or agent?

My rule: if the extraction can be written as a checklist or graph, make it a workflow; if it must run every day, turn it into code; if it requires fresh judgement, let an agent inspect and propose the next step. That same distinction is showing up in public talks about what to leave to people, workflows and agents.

/claude-code-setup-mcp-hooks-skills-2026.title: My Claude Code Setup After 4 Months of Daily Use (2026)
/claude-code-setup-mcp-hooks-skills-2026.description: My practical Claude Code setup after four months of daily use: native install, CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, hooks, skills, subagents, and what I kept.
/claude-code-setup-mcp-hooks-skills-2026.summaryHtml:
My Claude Code setup after four months of daily use

If I were setting up Claude Code again, I would keep the first version deliberately small: use the native installer, verify it, add one short CLAUDE.md, connect one MCP server in the narrowest useful scope, add one deterministic hook, and turn one repeated workflow into a skill. Add subagents only when a task needs isolated research or review context.

  1. Install. On macOS, Linux or WSL: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash. In Windows PowerShell: irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex. The native installer is Anthropic's recommended path in 2026.
  2. Verify. Run claude --version, then claude doctor, before debugging project configuration.
  3. Add project context. Start with one short CLAUDE.md containing only stable rules.
  4. Connect one tool. Use claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> and prove the server removes a real context switch before adding more.
  5. Automate and reuse. Add one deterministic hook, then move one repeated procedure into SKILL.md.

The useful part is not the size of the setup. It is being able to explain why every rule, server, hook, skill and subagent exists. The rest of this article shows the setup I actually used, what broke, and what I would keep.

Install and MCP commands checked against Anthropic's official setup, MCP, hooks, skills and subagents docs on August 1, 2026.
/claude-code-setup-mcp-hooks-skills-2026.faqHtml:
FAQ

What is the minimal Claude Code setup in 2026?

Start with the native Claude Code install, verify it with claude --version and claude doctor, add a short project CLAUDE.md, connect one MCP server, add one deterministic hook, and move one repeated procedure into a skill. Add subagents only when you need isolated context.

How do I install Claude Code on macOS, Linux or Windows?

On macOS, Linux or WSL, Anthropic recommends curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash. In Windows PowerShell, use irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex. Then run claude --version to verify the install.

How do I add an HTTP MCP server in Claude Code?

Use claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>, replacing the placeholders with a local label and the server endpoint. Local scope is the private default; use project scope only when the non-secret configuration should be shared through .mcp.json.

Are MCP servers and Claude Code hooks the same thing?

No. MCP servers expose external tools and data. Claude Code hooks run deterministic commands around events such as tool use, notifications, session lifecycle or compaction. Searchers sometimes call them “MCP hooks”, but they are separate layers.

Which Claude Code MCP server should I configure first?

Start with the server that removes your biggest manual context switch: repository tools, browser testing, deployment, a database or project memory. Add one, verify that Claude uses it correctly, then decide whether the next server is worth the context and security cost.

Should I use native Windows or WSL for Claude Code?

Use native Windows when the project and toolchain live in Windows. Use WSL when the project depends on Linux tools or sandboxing. Keep the shell, project files and Claude Code installation in the same environment instead of mixing paths.

Where are the official Claude Code docs?

Anthropic's current documentation covers installation, MCP servers, hooks, skills and subagents. This article adds a first-hand setup and trade-offs rather than replacing the official reference.

/claude-code-compaction-explained/.title: Claude Code /compact: What It Does, What Survives
/claude-code-compaction-explained/.description: Claude Code /compact explained: what context automatically compacted means, what survives compression, compact prompts, hooks and how to recover lost context.
/claude-code-compaction-explained/.summaryHtml:
Claude Code /compact: direct answers

When Claude Code reaches its context window limit, it compacts the conversation: older messages become a shorter summary so the session can continue. Project files stay unchanged, but details that only lived in chat can disappear from the active context.

QuestionDirect answer
What happens when Claude Code reaches its context window limit?Claude Code automatically compacts older conversation history into a summary. The project and files are not compressed; the risk is losing chat-only detail.
What does /compact do in Claude Code?It triggers compaction manually. Use it at a task boundary after saving rules, decisions, changed files and next checks to durable project files.
/compact vs /clear vs a new session?/compact continues with a summary. /clear removes the current conversation from active context. Start a new session when the task or assumptions have changed and you want a clean boundary.

/telegram-mcp-server-guide/.description: Telegram MCP Server guide for Claude Code: Telethon, MTProto, Bot API limits, FastMCP architecture, userbot safety, allowlists and audit logs.
/telegram-mcp-server-guide/.summaryHtml:
Quick answer: Telegram MCP Server in Claude Code

A Telegram MCP Server is a tool bridge, not just another Telegram bot. It lets an agent call Telegram operations through MCP, usually backed by Telethon/MTProto for user-session workflows or the Bot API for safer bot-scoped actions.

LayerUse it forBoundary
Bot APIBot-visible messages, commands and safer product flows.No full user account surface; limited channel/member access.
Telethon / MTProtoUser-session automation, reading chats you can access, richer Telegram methods.Higher account and privacy risk; needs strict allowlists.
MCP serverExpose Telegram actions as typed tools to Claude Code or another agent.Every tool needs naming, limits, logging and permission checks.
Audit logRecord what the agent read, drafted or sent.Do not store raw private chats as public source material.
/telegram-mcp-server-guide/.faqHtml:
FAQ

Is a Telegram MCP Server the same as a Telegram bot?

No. A bot is one Telegram account type and interface. An MCP server is the bridge that exposes Telegram capabilities to an AI agent as tools. It can be backed by the Bot API, Telethon/MTProto, or both.

When should I use Telethon instead of the Bot API?

Use Telethon only when you need user-session features that the Bot API does not expose. For production product flows, the Bot API is usually safer and easier to reason about.

What is the biggest security risk?

Unbounded send/read access. Start with read-only tools, chat allowlists, dry-run for sending, and logs that show exactly what the agent attempted.

Can Claude Code manage Telegram through MCP?

Yes, but give it narrow tools: search messages, draft a reply, summarize a channel, or send only to approved chats. “Full Telegram access” is not a feature; it is a liability.

/deploy-meilisearch-with-dokku-for-produ.description: Deploy MeiliSearch with Dokku in production: app setup, domain, master key, persistent storage, Docker deployment, Python indexing example, and security notes.
/deploy-meilisearch-with-dokku-for-produ.summaryHtml:
Quick answer: MeiliSearch works well on Dokku when you treat it as a stateful service: set a master key, mount persistent storage, put it behind HTTPS, and keep indexing code separate from the public search endpoint. The risky parts are secrets, backups, and accidental open admin APIs.

  • Use a strong master key and never expose it to the browser.
  • Persist the data directory before importing documents.
  • Plan backups before the search index becomes production-critical.
/deploy-meilisearch-with-dokku-for-produ.faqHtml:
FAQ

Can MeiliSearch run as a simple Dokku app?

Yes, but only if you persist the data directory and configure the master key. Otherwise a redeploy or dyno reset can wipe the index.

Should the frontend call MeiliSearch directly?

Only with a restricted search key. Admin keys and indexing keys should stay server-side.

/how-to-get-a-telegram-channel-subscribe.summaryHtml:
Quick answer: can you get a Telegram channel subscribers list?

Use the Bot API for a count. For a list, an authorized Telethon session can sample the participants Telegram makes visible. A public channel URL alone gives you no guarantee of list access or coverage.

What you needWhat to useWhat it returns
Subscriber countBot API getChatMemberCountA number for a channel the bot can access.
One known userBot API getChatMember with a user IDMembership status. Lookups for other users are only guaranteed when the bot is an admin.
Visible members in a channel you administerTelethon iter_participants with a limitA bounded sample. Visibility depends on the session and Telegram permissions.
Full list for another public channelAsk its administratorA public channel handle does not grant participant access.
/how-to-get-a-telegram-channel-subscribe.relatedHtml:
Related Telegram automation notes

If you are building real Telegram automation, read the Telegram MCP Server guide for Telethon/MTProto production patterns and the Telegram Stories Python guide for another user-session automation example. For market context, see the Telegram AI bots dataset.
/how-to-get-a-telegram-channel-subscribe.faqHtml:
FAQ: Telegram channel subscribers in Python

Can I export all subscribers from a Telegram channel with Python?

Telethon can return participants visible to your account. A successful sample does not establish that all subscribers are accessible, even if you administer the channel.

Does the Telegram Bot API return a channel subscribers list?

It provides a member count and a lookup for a known user ID. There is no Bot API method that enumerates channel subscribers.

Can I get subscribers from someone else’s public channel?

Only when Telegram grants your session access to those participants. Expect permission errors in channels you do not administer.

/how-to-watch-telegram-stories-from-pyth.description: Use Python + Telethon to watch Telegram Stories from a user session: detect active stories, call ReadStoriesRequest, and understand viewer-list/rate-limit caveats.
/how-to-watch-telegram-stories-from-pyth.summaryHtml:
Quick answer: watch Telegram Stories with Python

Yes, a Python script can watch Telegram Stories when it logs in as a real user session through Telethon/MTProto, not through the Bot API. The practical flow is: collect chats you can access, find users with active stories, call functions.stories.ReadStoriesRequest, and treat viewer visibility, rate limits and account risk as part of the product.

Looking for an anonymous Telegram Stories viewer? This is not one. This guide is for developers using Python and Telethon with a logged-in account; views can appear in the Story owner's viewer list.

QuestionShort answer
Can a bot do it?No. Telegram Stories are a user-account / MTProto surface, not a normal Bot API feature.
What does the script use?Telethon, iter_dialogs, iter_participants, stories_max_id, and ReadStoriesRequest.
Will the owner see me?Assume yes: watching a Story can put your account into the viewer list.
Should you masswatch?Only if you understand privacy, consent, rate limits and ban risk. This is not a stealth-growth hack.

Telegram story viewer vs this Python/Telethon script

Most pages ranking for Telegram story viewer offer an anonymous online viewer or downloader. This guide logs in as your own Telegram user through Telethon and calls the official stories.readStories method. Treat that user-account action as a visible Story view.

If anonymous viewing is the goal, Telegram documents Premium Stealth Mode in the official app. The Python example below does not activate Stealth Mode or promise anonymity. Use it for developer workflows where you control the account and accept the visibility, privacy and rate-limit boundaries.

/how-to-watch-telegram-stories-from-pyth.faqHtml:
FAQ: Telegram Stories automation from Python

Can I watch Telegram Stories from Python?

Yes, but not as a regular Telegram bot. You need a logged-in user session through Telethon/MTProto, then you can detect active Stories and mark them as read with Telegram Stories API calls.

Which Telethon call reads Telegram Stories?

The key call is functions.stories.ReadStoriesRequest. In the example below, the script checks user.stories_max_id and passes that max id to mark available Stories as read.

Can people see that my account viewed their Telegram Story?

Assume yes. Telegram Story owners can have a viewer list, so story viewing automation should be treated as visible user-account activity, not anonymous scraping.

Can the Bot API watch Telegram Stories?

No. The normal Bot API is not the right interface for watching user Stories. This kind of automation relies on a user session and MTProto, which is why the example uses Telethon.

Is mass story viewing safe?

It is risky if you run it like spam. Add delays, logs and strict limits, respect privacy and platform rules, and expect rate limits or account restrictions if you automate aggressively.

/claude-code-compaction-kak-rabotaet/.description: Что делает /compact в Claude Code: как сжимается контекст, что переживает compaction, что теряется, когда запускать вручную и как страховаться через CLAUDE.md, skills и hooks.
/claude-code-compaction-kak-rabotaet/.summaryHtml:
Короткий ответ: что делает /compact в Claude Code

/compact сжимает историю разговора в structured summary, чтобы Claude Code продолжил работу внутри context window. Полный transcript после этого уже не доступен модели как раньше: остаются выводы, текущая задача и часть важных решений. Критические правила лучше хранить в CLAUDE.md, skills и проектных файлах, а не в начале длинного чата.

ВопросКороткий ответ
Когда запускать?На границе задач: после debug, плана, PR или большого research-блока.
Что переживает?System prompt, root CLAUDE.md, текущая задача, последние важные выводы.
Что может потеряться?Старые детали, path-specific правила, snippets, причины промежуточных решений.
Как страховаться?Писать checkpoints в файлы и использовать PreCompact/PostCompact hooks.

/claude-code-compaction-kak-rabotaet/.faqHtml:
FAQ про /compact и compaction

Что такое compacting conversation в Claude Code?

Это момент, когда Claude Code заменяет длинную историю сессии кратким summary, чтобы освободить место в context window. После этого агент продолжает работу не с полным логом разговора, а с его сжатым представлением.

Чем /compact отличается от /clear?

/compact сохраняет сжатое summary текущей сессии и позволяет продолжить работу. /clear начинает разговор заново и убирает прежнюю историю из активного контекста.

Что делать, если Claude Code после compaction забыл важное правило?

Не пытайся держать критичные ограничения только в чате. Перенеси их в root CLAUDE.md, project notes, tasks, skill или hook-generated checkpoint, а затем попроси агента перечитать этот файл.

Можно ли отключить auto-compaction?

Практически лучше не бороться с самим механизмом, а управлять моментом сжатия: запускать /compact вручную на границе задач и сохранять checkpoints до длинных операций. Если задача пошла в неверную сторону, откат/rewind обычно полезнее, чем compact.

Quick answer: which March 2026 AI tools survived?

The useful March tools were not the flashiest demos. I kept the ones that made agent work more observable or easier to plug into a real workflow: paperclip for task state, gstack for review-style prompts, conductor.build as an IDE experiment, x402 as an API/payment primitive, and agent-browser plus Chrome debug port for real web QA.

/ai-tools-march-2026-honest-review/.faqHtml:
FAQ

Is this a list of the best AI tools of March 2026?

No. It is a field note from tools I actually tried. The question is not “what is trending?”, but “what survived contact with Claude Code, Codex, browser QA and real project work?”

Paperclip vs gstack: what is the difference?

Paperclip is more about visible task state for agents. Gstack is more about structured review and prompt workflows. One helps you see the work; the other helps you challenge the work.

Why include agent-browser and Chrome debug port?

Because agentic coding breaks down when the agent cannot see the product. Browser control, screenshots and debug-port access turn a vague “check the page” instruction into something verifiable.

Why mention x402 in an AI dev-tools review?

Because agent workflows eventually hit payment, API access and machine-to-machine transactions. x402 was not a daily coding tool for me, but it pointed at the infrastructure layer agents will need.

/always-on-ai-agent-server-setup/.description: How to run an AI agent 24/7 on a server: Claude Code-style loop, Telegram interface, cron jobs, durable memory, health checks and safety boundaries.
/always-on-ai-agent-server-setup/.summaryHtml:
Quick answer: how to run an AI agent 24/7

An always-on AI agent is not just Claude Code left open in a terminal. It needs a persistent runtime, a message interface, durable memory, scheduled jobs, logs, restart behaviour and strict boundaries for what it can read or write.

LayerWhat I use it forFailure mode
Server runtimeKeep the agent reachable when the laptop is closed.Process dies silently or loses home/session state.
Telegram interfaceVoice/text commands, DM triage and mobile control.Unbounded sending or wrong chat access.
Durable memoryProject facts, preferences and handoffs across sessions.Raw logs/secrets get stored instead of distilled facts.
Cron jobsSEO checks, monitoring, reminders and recurring reports.Jobs recurse, spam or run without enough context.
Health checksRestart and alert when the agent or bridge is down.You think it is working because no one told you it broke.
/always-on-ai-agent-server-setup/.faqHtml:
FAQ

Can Claude Code run 24/7 on a VPS?

Yes, but treat it as a supervised server agent, not an interactive terminal you forgot to close. Put the loop behind Docker or systemd, keep credentials in scoped environment variables, route commands through Telegram or a queue, and write durable memory/checkpoints outside the model context.

Can I run an AI agent 24/7 without a VPS?

Only if you have another machine that is always online. A laptop works for experiments, but sleep, network changes and local credentials make it fragile. A small VPS or home server is the boring reliable option.

Is this the same as a Telegram bot?

No. Telegram is just the interface. The useful part is the server-side agent loop: tools, memory, scheduled tasks, logs, and permissions that survive a single chat session.

How do you keep a 24/7 agent safe?

Use allowlists, scoped tools, dry-run modes for risky actions, audit logs, and a rule that raw secrets and private exports never become durable memory. The agent should not have broad write access just because it can receive messages.

What should I monitor first?

Monitor process uptime, queue failures, Telegram bridge errors, cron job exits and disk usage. Silent failure is worse than a noisy crash.
